$comment: Provenance for every external dataset in this repository. Each entry records where the data came from, what licence it carries, what we take from it, and how to refresh it. `scripts/refresh-sources.ts` reads this file.

sources.name: Free Exercise DB
usedIn: registry/movements.json (856 imported entries, tagged source: free-exercise-db)
sources.notes: Public domain, so it imposes no obligations on anything it is merged into. This is why it is the base layer.

sources.name: Garmin Connect exercise catalogue
sources.notes: Garmin publishes no licence for this. We keep it because interoperating with Connect is impossible without the exact enum values, which are facts about an interface rather than creative work. Treat redistribution as unresolved rather than settled. The endpoint returns 403 without a Connect session, so refreshing means opening the URL in a logged-in browser and saving the response.

sources.name: Garmin Connect strength benchmarks
provides: the lifts Connect tracks a 1RM for
sources.notes: Decides whether `@ 85% 1RM` can resolve to a real weight on a device. The endpoint returns 403 without a Connect session, so refreshing means opening the URL in a logged-in browser and saving the response.

sources.name: python-garminconnect workout payloads
sources.notes: Its comment describing weightValue as grams is wrong; a natively created workout shows the value is in the unit weightUnit names. See docs/references/README.md.

sources.name: Zwift .zwo workout files
provides: real third-party workouts as a cross-format oracle
sources.notes: Used as test fixtures, not shipped as product data. Each file states its own segment durations, which is what makes it an oracle.

sources.name: GoldenCheetah test workouts
provides: .erg and .mrc courses as a cross-format oracle
sources.notes: Test fixtures only. If the licence ever matters, these are trivially regenerable from any ERG source.

sources.name: Garmin FIT SDK workout examples
provides: canonical FIT workout binaries covering steps, repeats, and custom targets

sources.name: Sheiko #29 training block
provides: percentage-based strength prescriptions with a published number-of-lifts oracle
sources.notes: Prescriptions are factual training data. Kept verbatim in Sheiko's own notation so the rep totals stay independently derivable.

sources.name: Garmin FIT SDK Profile
sources.redistributable: the spec is public; we keep only the enum values we use
provides: every FIT message and type, including wkt_step_duration, wkt_step_target, intensity, file and sport
sources.notes: This is the official specification, and unlike the Connect JSON API it is public. All 22 enum values our FIT exporter writes were verified against it — every one matched, including duration_type 29 (reps), which we had earlier and wrongly claimed did not exist.

sources.name: Everkinetic exercise data
sources.notes: Share-alike. Merged into the canonical corpus at the user's direction with licensing deferred; every record names its sources so the decision stays reversible.

sources.name: wger exercise database
sources.notes: The only source carrying translations. Fetch with scripts/fetch-wger.py, which pages slowly and resumes: wger runs a small public instance. Two earlier notes here were wrong. The API does not time out — it responds in well under a second. And the failure is not DNS resolution order: forcing ipv4first changes nothing. Node cannot reach this host by either route in this environment (undici gives UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, the core https module gives ECONNRESET) while curl and Python's urllib both succeed. Two different failure modes from two different Node clients suggests TLS negotiation, but that is unconfirmed.

candidates.name: Strength Level exercise catalogue
candidates.licence: proprietary; automated access prohibited by the site's Terms and Conditions
candidates.status: declined 2026-08-22 on terms; measured the same day, which did not change the answer
candidates.notes: Researched as a sixth source for names, aliases and muscle data, and declined. https://strengthlevel.com/terms-and-conditions § "Automated Access and API Usage" (last updated 2025-01-23) prohibits, unless authorized in writing: automated means "to access, query or otherwise collect information from the Service"; access through "APIs that haven't been officially published" — /api/exercises is undocumented, so it is exactly that; and systematically downloading, storing or copying any content. robots.txt says `Allow: /`, which is a crawl directive and not a licence, and does not survive the contract. Strength Level Limited is a UK company selling subscriptions against this data. Same disposition and same reason as `musclewiki` below. The only lawful route is written authorization or a partnership, at the Company's discretion — support@strengthlevel.com. MEASURED 2026-08-22 (a-z + 0-9, serial, 2s apart; digits return nothing) to price the decision, not to reopen it: 290 distinct exercises under standard=true; limit=256 is not a cap (largest letter 254, and limit=1000 returns the same 254); all fields 100% populated except aliases at 40.7%; the response also carries id and name, which the documented exercise.fields list does not ask for. Against our 3120: 197 already held, 0 of the 137 muscle-data gaps closed (they are stretches and mobility; this is a strength-standards catalogue), 55 genuinely new aliases of which 24 land on core movements, and 93 unresolved of which 62 are near-matches on spelling rather than new movements. bodypart is one coarse label from nine values and cannot fill muscleClaims[source] = {primary, secondary} honestly. The `count` field — real logged lifts, Bench Press 48.7M — is the popularity signal queue item 4 actually wants and is the most proprietary thing on the endpoint. Full write-up and the reasoning in docs/context/deliberately-not-done.md; the alias hole it measured is queue item 8.

candidates.name: ExerciseDB
candidates.notes: Largest catalogue found, but the AGPL covers the API code and the data's own licence is not stated. Would need clarifying before use.

candidates.name: EMG activation studies
candidates.notes: The only source of *measured* rather than editorially assigned muscle involvement. No consolidated open dataset exists — it is per-study, heterogeneous in protocol, and covers a few hundred exercises at most. Valuable as targeted evidence for a small set of movements; unusable as a bulk import.

mergedCorpora.registry/movements.canonical.json: 3120 movements from garmin, free-exercise-db, wger, everkinetic and wdl-curated. 2983 carry muscle data, 1503 a Garmin mapping, 621 a name in another language, 178 marked core.
mergedCorpora.registry/workouts.canonical.json: 202 workouts with source text, parsed AST and derived summary.
